items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: We did a concert once with the San Antonio Symphony... with Ella and she was on — Ella, Bill Basie’s band, and quite a decent period with the San Antonio orchestra.

ctx.x: You might travel a three or four hundred mile radius.

Yeah, that would be it, yeah. I played with three or four of those bands. Unbelievable. They were all bad, but this was a great learning process. In fact I played with a band, his name was Buddy Fisher, another — he imitated Ben Burney. I don’t know how he ever came about that but he talked and he spoke lyrics and thought he was such a star in front of the band. And we played Kansas City at the Muhlbach Hotel and I went down to the very famous street and met a guy by the name of Bill Basie, who had a seven piece…

“F Sharp Henderson.” That was my name, the rest of my life, wherever I would see him. We did a concert once with the San Antonio Symphony, which was one of the greatest memories of my life, believe it or not with Ella and she was on — Ella, Bill Basie’s band, and quite a decent period with the San Antonio orchestra. It was one of the greatest nights, music nights, I just sat there like you’re living in Valhalla, but nobody came. I couldn’t believe it. It was a benefit but they put up a sign and said here they…
